title: ORT env creation logs 'Init provider bridge failed.' in winml venv
head: 2724c4cd
stderr_excerpt: [W:onnxruntime:Default, onnxruntime_pybind_module.cc:45 onnxruntime::python::CreateOrtEnv] Init provider bridge failed.
impact: Unknown-but-bounded: all observed GPU executions succeed despite it; treated as warning-to-audit, not harmless-by-assumption.
observation: The warning is emitted once per process at onnxruntime import/env creation in .venv-winml, BEFORE any amdgpu-ep.dll registration and independent of it. Also seen in G1-era runs. GPU sessions still create and execute (canary cand[1] OK; G2/G3 32/32 receipts).
hypotheses: ORT python bridge tries to preload a provider bridge DLL that is absent in the windowsml distribution (cosmetic, no functional effect)
Bridge init failure disables some provider surface we have not used yet (e.g. direct AMDGPUExecutionProvider class registration)
next_discriminating_experiment: Fresh process: import onnxruntime with ORT log level verbose and capture which bridge init is attempted; compare providers surface with/without the warning. Bounded: 3 runs.

title: MIGraphX auto_save_problem_cache write fails (WindowsApps protected path)
head: 2724c4cd
exception: auto_save_problem_cache: save failed: write_buffer: Failure opening file: C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\...\ExecutionProvider\problem_cache.json
impact: Possible slower session-create across processes; no execution or parity failure observed. Never modify WindowsApps/ACLs (forbidden).
observation: Emitted by the AMDGPU EP when a graph compiles in our process: the bundled MIGraphX attempts to persist its problem cache next to the MSIX DLL under WindowsApps, which is ACL-protected (read/execute for user). Emitted 3x during one canary session-create+run. Compilation and execution still succeed.
hypotheses: External root cause: MSIX package does not relocate its cache dir; expected user-writable path is not configured by this EP build (ep_options empty, no documented option on 1.8.65.0)
Consequence is cold-compile cost per process (no persistent cache), not correctness
next_discriminating_experiment: Measure session-create wall time in N=3 fresh processes vs repeated in-process creates; if flat, cache miss cost is bounded to first compile per process. Check whether MIGRAPHX_* env vars are honored (child-process env only, no system change).

title: AMDGPU ep-device candidate[0] fails with HIP 101 invalid device ordinal (GPU=0)
head: 2724c4cd
exception: [ONNXRuntimeError] : 1 : FAIL : HIP failure 101: invalid device ordinal; GPU=0; file=C:\j\amdgpu-ep\src\shared\hip\allocator.cc; line=14; expr=hipSetDevice(device_id)
impact: Candidate[0] unusable for every model; harness works around via fail-closed candidate loop (never a silent skip). GPU work happens on candidate[1]. Root cause is inside the closed vendor DLL — external boundary.
observation: With 2 AMDGPU OrtEpDevices enumerated (global indices 3 and 4 of 5), session creation on candidate[0] deterministically raises HIP 101 at hipSetDevice(device_id=0) inside the vendor EP; candidate[1] succeeds and profiles AMDGPU compute. Reproduced live 2026-11-17T21:49Z (canary) and consistent with G1-era behavior (dev[0] HIP 101, dev[1] OK).
hypotheses: The two OrtEpDevices both target the single physical iGPU but the EP assigns HIP ordinals 0/1; ordinal 0 is invalid in this driver+EP combination (only ordinal 1 backed), i.e. EP enumeration bug
Ordinal space is offset by the other 3 non-AMDGPU ep-devices; candidate index != HIP device id and cand[0] maps to a nonexistent id
GameViewer virtual display reorders/offsets device enumeration
next_discriminating_experiment: Independent short-lived processes x3: enumerate ep devices, attempt cand[0] then cand[1], record HIP error text GPU=n per candidate. If GPU=0 always for cand[0] and GPU=1 for cand[1] => enumeration-offset hypothesis strengthened; then try reversing device order to check ordinal assignment stability.

title: Dual AMDGPU ep-device enumeration indistinguishable; legacy receipts stored DXGI-0 LUID not the bound ep-device
head: 2724c4cd
impact: Identity claims in legacy receipts must be downgraded to EP_DEVICE_SELECTED(probe-evidenced) + DXGI corroboration only; PHYSICAL_GPU_IDENTITY_CORROBORATED requires new R1-C evidence.
observation: Both AMDGPU OrtEpDevices expose IDENTICAL ep_vendor/ep_options/ep_metadata (library_path, version 0.1.0) — no LUID, ordinal, or adapter hint. Old G2/G3 receipts record session.device_luid from the DXGI adapter chosen BEFORE the probe (index 0 -> 0x0:0x11746) while the session actually bound ep-device candidate[1]; therefore the legacy device_luid field is DXGI corroboration, NOT binding evidence. Identical name/VID/DID does not prove the two DXGI LUIDs (two enumerations of the same iGPU) map 1:1 to ep-device candidates.
hypotheses: The physical 8060S is one GPU enumerated twice; ep candidates are two HAL views (one broken per RCA-003) — binding to cand[1] still lands on the only physical GPU, but this must be PROVEN, not assumed
Candidates could map to the two DXGI enumerations in unknown order
next_discriminating_experiment: R1-C: per-candidate probe in isolated processes capturing profile counts + memory telemetry; correlate with DXGI/PnP evidence; if candidates remain indistinguishable, mark IDENTITY_BINDING_UNPROVEN for candidate->LUID mapping and record selection attestation instead.
